text:
Ava (CFO): Thanks for attending today	Dropping a follow-up thread for runway/burn Qs and procurement clarifications. Post short Qs and well reply here. :memo:

morgan (eng): Quick Q  how exactly are we calculating runway now? Is it base burn or adjusted for hiring plans?

Ava (CFO): We report runway as 'months of runway at projected burn'. That means we start with current cash balance and divide by projected monthly outflow. Projected outflow = base payroll + benefits + approved hiring ramp (only roles with an offer accepted and start date entered) + committed infra/contracts (amortized over contract term). We also apply a 3-month trailing smoothing window to avoid noisy spikes.

alex (product): Is the Dedicated reserved capacity purchase from last week included?

Ravi (Finance Ops): If the procurement ticket has an issued PO or the contract has been signed and recorded in AP, its included. If its still in negotiation, its excluded until the PO is created.

jamal (sales): Are we pausing hiring velocity? Heard different things in GMs meeting.

Sofia (People): No hiring freeze. We are tightening prioritization: all non-critical roles go through the hiring committee. Senior IC and manager roles need extra calibration this quarter.

morgan (eng): Procurement delays last quarter were painful. Any SLA for infra vendors?

olivia (procurement): We're launching a "fast-track" path for infra, cloud, and strategic ISV partners: target turnaround = 7 business days from request if vendor provides standard security docs (SOC2, ISO) and master service agreement. Custom legal redlines or bespoke invoices will fall back to normal cycles. Please tag @olivia on the Jira request to escalate.

morgan (eng): Where do we submit fast-track requests?

procurement-bot: New vendor requests -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/secure/QuickCreate select 'Vendor Onboarding'. Use label: fast-track. Updates post automatically to #vendors.

Ava (CFO): A few policy bullets: 
- P-card thresholds: engineers $2,000, managers $10,000 for non-capex software.
- Any one-time spend > $50,000 or multi-year commits > $50,000 need pre-approval from Finance + Legal (create PO request).
- Capitalizable infra purchases follow capex guidelines; contact Finance Ops for classification.

alex (product): Can teams trial low-cost SaaS without PO?

Ravi (Finance Ops): Yes for trials <$500/month. Register the trial in the central tracker so we avoid duplicate subscriptions. For purchases that convert to paid >$500/month within 90 days, raise a procurement ticket.

olivia (procurement): Small SaaS intake: https://forms.gle/rdw-small-saas — include estimated seats, expected ARR if converted, and security contact.

jamal (sales): What about invoice timing? When are vendor payments processed vs customer invoicing?

Ravi (Finance Ops): AP runs Tue/Thu. For urgent vendor payments (critical vendors or close-of-cycle) open an "AP expedite" ticket with PO and business justification. Customer invoicing runs EOM; collections post as payments arrive.

morgan (eng): If a vendor asks for a large setup fee that tips us over $50k, should we pause implementation until approval?

Ava (CFO): Not necessarily. We have an Emergency Spend path for customer-impacting or uptime-critical purchases. Create an "Emergency Spend" ticket, tag @Ava and @Ravi, provide vendor name, ticket ID, and reason. We can approve same-day on a case-by-case basis; keep usage rare.

Sofia (People): Reminder: any contract tied to headcount must include People in approvals so we can align start dates and ramp assumptions for forecasting.

morgan (eng): Can you share the short doc that spells out the "projected burn" formula?

Ravi (Finance Ops): Posted: https://drive.redwood.com/finance/projected-burn-qna. It lists inputs (salaries, benefits, committed infra amortization, one-time capex treatment) and the smoothing method.

olivia (procurement): Ill publish a 1-pager fast-track playbook and the ticket templates to #vendors later today.

Ava (CFO): If youre blocked on a vendor or contract, reply with vendor name + Jira ticket and well triage. Thanks everyone for the focused questions — well keep this thread live for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
